description.narrative: Iraq has been experiencing many years of violent conflict. This has caused a shrinking of civic space, deteriorating human rights situation, unresolved past conflict and gender inequality. The SCC program in Iraq will address the damaged inter-community relations and the relation between state and citizens. Thereby empowering survivors and victims of violence to advocate for their rights with regards to justice and accountability. The main focus of the program lies on the Ninewa governorate, which was hit hardest by ISIL. Capacity-building training will be provided focusing on human rights, gender, dealing with the past, and advocacy.

The activity is part of a larger programme implemented by the Strengthening Civil Courage Alliance, consisting of ABAAD – Resource Center for Gender Equality, Amnesty International The Netherlands, DefendDefenders, PAX and their partner networks.

The main objective is to reach evidence-based advocacy of strong and diverse victim groups and other civil society group in Iraq, that contribute to the realisation of inclusive transformative justice processes and to the nun-recurrence of atrocities. More specifically, the program aims for the victims and survivors of human rights abuses and violent conflict in Ninewa to influence transformative justice and accountability processes to be more inclusive. Secondly, the goal is to reach an increased collaboration between inclusive victim and survivor groups across the political divide, and finally, the programme aims to strengthen international standards and due diligence on arms export control.

The target groups are marginalised survivor and victim groups; Iraqi partner organisations; grantees, such as community-based organisations; a network of advocates; local and provincial authorities; national authorities; and international policymakers.

title.narrative: Iraqi partners have improved their understanding of safety and inclusion in their work environment, have changed their Codes of Conduct to promote a safe and inclusive working environment and have implemented these changes
# of CSOs using a Gender and Social Inclusion lens during all phases of the programming cycle with specific attention to youth.

description.narrative: In all phases of the programming cycle (planning, designing, implementing, monitoring, evaluation), CSOs take steps to improve the participation of marginalized people (especially women, girls, and youth), and consider how to dismantle the attitudes, laws, customs, and institutions that sustain the exclusion of marginalized people)

comment.narrative: Both Iraqi partners employ a number of women and youth, who are then also involved in different stages of programming. However, 'hard' decision making - e.g. on staff and employment, budget, and shifts in strategic focus - are in reality made by select number of senior staff members, typically men aged 40 and older.

In 2022, the plan is to identify the gaps for each partner, and translate these into concrete action points to tackle on an internal level - therefore elaborating an action plan with a respective mechanism to monitor its implementation.

Following trainings and workshops by the alliance partners in 2022, two CSOs have both demonstrated the willingness and ability to include all marginalized community members in the activities of the project, taking into account intersectional sensitivities and representation and retaining a trauma-sensitive approach. This was mostly evident during coordination calls and trainings, and in quarterly reports submitted by Iraqi partners. Gender advisors of both partners demonstrated a sensible increase in intersectional feminist approaches to activity programming, and this was evident in the effective coaching of grantees and subsequent implemented activities. A concrete follow-up action plan on PSEAH to introduce internal policies at both organizations to concretize the work towards this objective will be set in 2023. ABAAD will take the lead on this.
Iraqi partners have developed an action plan to develop new policies to ensure PSEA (followed-up by ABAAD)

In April 2024, ABAAD conducted a PSEA Training of Trainers (ToT) for 15 participants in Erbil as a follow-up to the PSEA Coaching and Mentoring workshop held in August 2023 for two NGOs (Al-Mesalla and PFO). The training aimed to enhance the sustainability of the initiative by equipping participants with the skills to deliver PSEA training within their organizations and communities. After the delivery of these essential concepts, working group sessions with each organization was set to finalize the final points in the action plan of the Coaching and Mentoring exercise.

Design one action plan per partner for improving integrity practices using PSEAH tools elaborated during an ABAAD training. PAX will coordinate closely between Abaad and the partners to elaborate concrete action plans to improve HR practices, staff accountability, feedback and staff development mechanisms, and diversity and inclusion.

In Q2 2023, Abaad conducted an updated PSEA assessment with the partners. In August 2023, Abaad conducted a training with key staff from PFO and Al Mesalla for a refresher on PSEA principles, policies, and means of implementation. Following the workshop, each organization participated in a 1-day workshop with ABAAD, where staff developed an action plan tailored to the needs of their organizations, including a timeline. One PSEA focal point per organization was appointed to follow-up and report on the progress of the action plan
No increased level planned for 2021.

While no concrete implementation has been done yet, PAX and partners have launched the initiative to develop one action plan per Iraqi partner to drastically improve accountability and safety mechanisms within each organization. Following the PSEAH training, the two partner CSOs filled-in an extensive PSEAH self-assessment tool and shared it with the Alliance partners.

The policy has already been established in 2024 and the code of conduct has been updated by both Iraqi partners followed-up by PAX & ABAAD. In 2025 we will work with both Iraqi partners on action plan and feedback mechanism to ensure policy implementation.

comment.narrative: National-level authorities (parliament) are seated/elected, but without acting government, no tangible action can be determined by Iraqi partners.

Goal is to be decided through strategy sessions with network of advocates (SO2), Iraqi partners, PAX, Amnesty, and knowledge partners. However, tentatively, the goal is to create direct interaction between grass-root/victim organizations or initiatives and national-level authorities (e.g. in Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Migration and Displacement, etc.), brokered by international- and Iraqi partners, the latter which will have a leading role. Change target is openness of Iraqi authorities to victims, which must increase over politically and exclusively oriented policy makers.

2022: National authorities have yet to be reached within the project. The newly appointed head of government is the previous commissioner for HR in Iraq, which will open up the space for more targeted action with national level-authorities in 2023. 2023: With the delay in the implementation of the advocacy component of the project, it was not yet possible to facilitate lobby and advocacy meetings between the network of advocates and national authorities in Baghdad. Advocates and grantees have first started targeting local authorities and actors to gain influence and trust on the local level. In 2024 and as partners advance through the advocacy strategy timeline, advocates will start targeting national level actors, with the aim to influence the national agenda. 2024: Following visits to the Ninewa Governorate Office to discuss three key issues—compensation, reopening of mass graves in Sinjar, and digitalization of government directorates—official letters were issued by the Ninewa Provincial Council. These were directed to the Martyrs Foundation and the Directorate of Mass Graves Affairs in Baghdad, requesting action on reopening Sinjar’s mass grave cases and adopting recommendations on digitalization and the compensation process. As a result, the Directorate of Mass Graves Affairs responded positively. This year, their teams reached Sinjar and South Mosul to investigate and begin the process of opening previously neglected mass graves. DNA testing has also been initiated for the purpose of victim identification. This marks a significant achievement. A detailed ‘story of change’ has been documented; for more information, please refer to the narrative report.

title.narrative: # of times that Iraqi partner CSOs succeed in creating space for CSO demands and positions through agenda setting, influencing the debate and/ or creating space to engage (SCS3)

comment.narrative: One Iraqi partner regularly engages with national-level authorities on priorities emerging from civil society gatherings and projects, including those with PAX. Topics include freedom and protection of activists and the YPS 2250 agenda. Another Iraqi partner is less active on the national level (assumption). This needs to be further clarified through the L&A assessment, planned for July 2022 (target starts 2023).

For sub-national level authorities, the goal is to 'recruit' them as allies (representing their provincial citizen constituencies) and to engage with them in accessing national level authorities with advocacy messages. Change target is openness of Iraqi authorities to victims and support their claims, which must increase over politically and exclusively oriented policy makers.

2022: Outcome harvesting conducted demonstrated how 1 grantee activity succeeded in receiving pledges from local authorities to advance work on compensation of victims to national levels 2023: In 2023, advocates and grantees have started targeting local authorities and actors to gain influence and trust on the local level. By the end of 2023 it was still too early to observe behavioral changes in local actors targeted by the network of advocates. Nonetheless, from the start of 2023, grantees began to involve local authorities in victim-led initiatives, where victims and affected community members shared their experiences and openly discussed their challenges and priorities for transitional justice. This engagement contributed to bridging the gap between local authorities and their communities at our project location, leading to significant behavioral changes. 9 harvested outcomes for 2023 showcase these behavorial changes in local actors, with 3 outcomes that highlighted concrete policy changes and agenda setting addressing the needs and priorities of affected local communities. 2024: In 2024, advocates and grantees continued targeting local authorities, leading to changed behavior in targeted actors such as improved treatment of victims by trained officials, relocation of survivor-related departments to safer spaces, enhanced logistical support for compensation procedures, regular provincial council meetings with survivors, and steps towards digital transformation in compensation services.

title.narrative: # of CSOs with increased L&A capacities

comment.narrative: AINL conducted intensive training on MDR process, and followed up by cloesly coaching with both Iraqi partners. Each partner has produced one comprehensive HR report based on documented cases (1 for PFO, 1 for Al Mesalla)

Due to delays in the Iraqi cabinet formation (see narrative report), all L&A activities and SO2 were delayed until end of 2022. L&A capacity assessment was conducted in November 2022. Trainings planned in Q1 2023. One CSO chose to strenghten capacity area "producing key messages"; another CSO chose to strenghten "producing evidence".

in 2023, the advocacy strategy of the project will be elaborated and implemented. The strategy includes tailor-made trainings for Iraqi partners in MDR, evidence-based advocacy, gender-sensitive messaging, research writing skills, and communication skills. Iraqi partners will themselves lead the advocacy work of the network of advocates according to their chosen capacity area: one CSO will be trained and will lead on producing tailored messages, while another CSO will be trained and will lead in producing evidence as resource for all the campaigns that will be held by the advocates. Targets per organization were set for 2023 in the framework of the L&A capacity development.

In mid-2023, PFO decided to change L&A capacity areas and choose A- capacity to produce evidence. This is due to the updated ToC and subsequent planning and division of responsibilties of the project. With both partners sharing the responsibility to lead on evidence-based advocacy, it was essential for PFO staff to increase their skills in that area in order to reach the project's set targets for SO2. PFO staff participated in all the trainings with Al Mesalla staff around capacity area A.
